questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the sources of raw materials, X and Y.

X .........

Y ......... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**X** supplies nitrogen: the **air** (nitrogen is separated from liquid air by fractional distillation).

**Y** supplies hydrogen: **natural gas (methane)**, which reacts with steam ($\mathrm{CH_4} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO} + 3\mathrm{H_2}$); water (steam) is the other source of hydrogen.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction occurring in the reactor.

(ii) What is the function of the Iron in the reactor?

(iii) How is the wastage of the unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen minimised? *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) $\mathrm{N_2(g)} + 3\mathrm{H_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH_3(g)}$ (reversible; check: 2 N and 6 H on each side).

(ii) Iron is a **catalyst**: it **speeds up the reaction** (lets equilibrium be reached faster at a reasonable temperature) without being used up; it does not change the yield.

(iii) The unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen, which stay as gases in the cooler, are **recycled**: they are returned to the reactor (as shown by the arrow in the diagram), so nothing is wasted.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the function of the cooler? ......... *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The cooler **condenses (liquefies) the ammonia** so that it separates from the unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen, which remain gases and are recycled.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The ammonia obtained is used to produce the nitrogen fertilizer, ammonium nitrate ($\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$) (RMM = 80).

(i) Name the substance that is reacted with ammonia to form ammonium nitrate.

(ii) Calculate the percentage of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Nitric acid** ($\mathrm{HNO_3}$): $\mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{HNO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$.

(ii) $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$ contains 2 nitrogen atoms: mass of nitrogen $= 2 \times 14.0 = 28.0$.

Percentage of nitrogen $= \dfrac{28.0}{80} \times 100 = \mathbf{35\%}$.
